data.why: Dexcom_Example_Subject_A.csv is a trimmed (~1 day, 300-row) excerpt of the repo's own Clarity export format, kept under size limits, with an injected sensor gap (05:05-05:30), a one-point outlier spike (410 mg/dL glitch), and a 'Low' sensor-flag reading so the preprocessing/interpolation and feature code is actually exercised; seed/config.ini restores the ID/Glucose/Timestamp column-name config that app.py expects to find next to itself (it only exists under glucose360/config.ini in this commit, so app.py would crash with KeyError on startup without it).

goals: Upload a CGM export (Dexcom, FreeStyle Libre, or custom-column CSV) and have it cleaned, resampled, and gap-interpolated into a per-subject glucose time series
Compute standard glycemic variability and time-in-range statistics (e.g. mean glucose, CV, GMI, % time in range) for each uploaded subject
Automatically detect curated hypoglycemic/hyperglycemic episodes and optionally bulk-import or hand-add meal/exercise events tied to a subject
Visualize a subject's glucose trace as daily, weekly, spaghetti, or AGP (Ambulatory Glucose Profile) plots and download them as PDF/HTML
Inspect a single event (e.g. a meal) and compute its localized metrics (AUC, iAUC, baseline, peak, nadir, delta) with an accompanying plot
Export computed features, event features, and the events table as CSV for downstream analysis or an AGP report as HTML

review.summary: The tree gets the tool's purpose right (clean CGM exports, compute glycemic metrics, annotate and measure events, plot and export) and the screens back up nearly every claim. Before filing, it needs the automatic episode detection and bulk event import added, phases ordered by the work rather than the tabs, two citations fixed, and the run's corrupted event edits flagged.
